description: The line plot illustrates the minimum final displacement error (minFDE₂₀) in meters as a function of the ratio of observed to total trajectory length for five different methods: TrajICL, Head Tuning, FT, LoRA 16, and LoRA 64. The x-axis, labeled "Ratio," represents the proportion of the trajectory observed, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 on a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The y-axis, labeled "minFDE₂₀ (←)," indicates the minimum final displacement error, ranging from 0.8 to 1.3 on a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The TrajICL method, represented by a blue line with circular markers, starts at a minFDE₂₀ of approximately 0.9 at a ratio of 0.0 and remains relatively stable, fluctuating slightly around 0.87 to 0.90 across the entire range. The Head Tuning method, shown with an orange line and circular markers, begins at a minFDE₂₀ of about 1.32 at a ratio of 0.0 and exhibits a steady decrease, reaching approximately 1.07 at a ratio of 1.0. The FT method, depicted with a green line and circular markers, starts at a minFDE₂₀ of roughly 1.08 at a ratio of 0.0 and decreases to about 0.75 at a ratio of 1.0. The LoRA 16 method, represented by a red line with circular markers, begins at a minFDE₂₀ of approximately 1.22 at a ratio of 0.0 and decreases to about 0.91 at a ratio of 1.0. The LoRA 64 method, shown with a purple line and circular markers, starts at a minFDE₂₀ of about 1.22 at a ratio of 0.0 and decreases to approximately 0.91 at a ratio of 1.0. All methods show a general trend of decreasing error as the observed trajectory ratio increases, with the FT method achieving the lowest error values across most of the ratio range.
